validated_results.title: Tea consumption: fluid intake and bladder cancer risk in Southern Taiwan.
validated_results.reason: Hospital-based case-control study of beverage intake reporting a separable qualitative finding for alcohol consumption and newly diagnosed bladder cancer incidence, although no numeric estimate is given in the abstract.

extraction.population: Patients with histologically confirmed, newly diagnosed bladder cancer and surgical hospital controls in two major hospitals in Kaohsiung

sample_size.excerpt: Using a structured questionnaire, a trained interviewer interviewed 40 patients and 160 controls.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 40 + 160 = 200

cases.excerpt: Compared with non-tea drinkers, the odds ratios of bladder cancer for oolong tea drinkers was 3.00 (95% CI 1.20 to 7.47); for non-oolong tea drinkers (black and/or other green tea), it was 14.86 (95% CI 2.13 to 103.83). The risk was greater among those who began to drink tea before age 40 (OR 9.50, 95% CI 2.39 to 37.75) and those who had been drinking tea for more than 30 years (OR 17.75, 95% CI 3.00 to 105.17).

design.excerpt: A case-control study was conducted in Kaohsiung, Taiwan between August 1996 and June 1997.

timing.excerpt: A case-control study was conducted in Kaohsiung, Taiwan between August 1996 and June 1997.

gender.excerpt: individually matched by sex, age, and date of admission
